segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics News Digest for November 24, 2026.
Today we cover SimScale AI for autonomous vehicles, robotics-in-a-box hardware, and funding for accessible robot hardware.
From Robotics & Automation News, Ati Robotics adopts SimScale AI simulation for autonomous vehicle development.
This report details the utilization of SimScale's AI-native cloud simulation technology to validate the hardware of the Sherpa autonomous mobile robot.
The engineering team employs SimScale for structural and mechanical simulations of the platform to ensure it meets factory-floor operational requirements.
This virtual testing allows for hardware performance investigation without the overhead of traditional simulation setups.
Furthermore, SimScale provides a shared simulation environment accessible to engineering teams operating in both the United States and India.
This adoption reflects a broader manufacturing trend toward increased automation to address labor shortages and boost overall efficiency in the sector.
This move signifies a progression in using advanced simulation for physical robotics validation.
The industry should observe further integration of cloud-based simulation for hardware development.
From Robotics & Automation News, ASRock Industrial launched the RBK-100 Robotics-in-a-Box to simplify physical artificial intelligence development.
This integrated platform provides researchers and developers with a unified system for hands-on experimentation with physical AI tasks.

The system incorporates the ASRock Industrial NUC BOX-358H equipped with an Intel Core Ultra X7 Processor 358H, alongside an RGB depth camera, a six-degrees-of-freedom robotic arm, and AiRoboStarter software.
This setup enables the execution of AI-based pick-and-place operations, data collection, and model training within a single workflow.
The platform also offers the optional capability for agentic AI integration to support multimodal robotic workflows.
This development points toward more accessible methods for bridging the gap between software AI and physical robotic execution.
From Robotics & Automation News, Coprod raises six million dollars in a pre-seed round to make robot hardware as easy to build as software.
The company is focused on simplifying the construction of robotic hardware by concentrating on compatible co:products.
This effort aims to reduce the time and expense associated with robotics development, which is frequently impeded by complex component integration.
The hardware components utilize a unified software application programming interface to standardize communication and ensure real-time performance across the system.
The raised funds will be allocated to launching initial components and setting up a facility for hardware prototyping.
Coprod intends to alleviate integration challenges in robotics by supplying hardware designed for ease of use.
This development signals a push toward more streamlined and accessible physical realization of complex robotic systems.
From Robotics & Automation News, Yarbo opens SDK beta to developers for modular yard robots.
This report details the release of a closed beta for the Software Development Kit to facilitate custom applications for the company's modular yard robots.
The SDK is a component of Yarbo's Open Platform strategy designed to allow users to customize robot interactions beyond the capabilities of existing hardware attachments.
Developers can utilize this kit to create applications and plugins that connect Yarbo devices with external systems such as smart home platforms and commercial software.
Potential applications demonstrated include integrating mowing data with irrigation systems, coordinating snow removal routines, and supporting academic research in autonomous navigation.
This initiative represents a progression toward an open robotics ecosystem that is anticipated to eventually incorporate a hardware development kit.
The development signals an expansion in how modular robotics are integrated into broader technological applications.
From Robotics & Automation News, Figure AI patents a wearable system for teaching humanoid robots through human movement.
This report details the patenting of a wearable robotic system designed to capture human arm movements for training or remotely controlling humanoid robots.
The system is constructed as a backpack frame featuring articulated arms outfitted with sensors to measure movements at the shoulder, elbow, and wrist.
This technology is engineered to capture data from routine tasks within working environments without necessitating motion-capture studios.
The system facilitates real-time control with a delay of less than twenty milliseconds.
This methodology provides an alternative means for collecting authentic, real-world training data for robotics through demonstrations from human workers.
The development signals a shift toward practical, in-situ data acquisition for advanced robotics training.
From Robotics & Automation News, "MassRobotics to open marine robotics facility at Boston Fish Pier".
This report details the development of a new marine robotics facility at Boston Fish Pier, which will provide startups with access to Boston Harbor for testing underwater robots.
Construction is currently underway as part of a partnership with Massport under the Blue Edge initiative to support the marine technology sector.
The facility is scheduled to open in early 2028, with industry programming commencing in 2027.

The site will enable companies to design and test prototypes in existing workshops before deploying them into the harbor, positioning Boston as a global center for marine robotics and supporting the Marine Tech Hub initiative.
This development indicates a significant expansion of testing infrastructure for marine robotics technology.
From Robotics & Automation News, ABB launches ‘world’s first’ industrial motor with built-in AI.
This report details the introduction of Intelleqt, a low-voltage motor featuring integrated artificial intelligence for real-time operational insights.
ABB has developed this solution to provide equipment-level intelligence, allowing motor data to be connected directly to existing digital platforms.
This technology establishes the necessary data foundation for scaling artificial intelligence-driven operations across various industrial sectors.
The implementation of Intelleqt is designed to enhance system reliability, increase productivity, and decrease unplanned downtime through actionable insights derived from motor performance.
ABB has scheduled a broader rollout of the Intelleqt technology commencing in 2027 across several international markets.
This development signals a significant step in embedding intelligence directly into physical machinery.
Further developments in industrial AI integration are anticipated.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: MOLA cloud: free online LiDAR SLAM from ROS bags, plus camera and LiDAR-camera calibration".
This report details the launch of MOLA cloud, a free online service enabling LiDAR SLAM and camera calibration directly within a web browser utilizing ROS 2 data.
The service allows users to upload ROS 2 bags to generate three-dimensional maps and process video or image sets to derive camera intrinsics.
It automates the extraction of point cloud maps, trajectory data, and the extrinsic LiDAR-camera calibration through an automated methodology.
The service operates on secure, isolated servers within the European Union and implements monthly usage restrictions.
This advancement offers a readily accessible method for complex spatial data processing and sensor fusion for developers.
Further development in this area indicates increased accessibility to advanced robotics data processing tools.
From The Robot Report, "How does Orchard AI fit into John Deere’s technology portfolio?".
This story details the integration of Orchard AI into John Deere’s technology portfolio to incorporate plant-level crop insights.
Orchard AI utilizes AI-powered cameras to analyze individual plants, generating detailed data concerning yield, fruit, and canopy structure.
This acquisition enables John Deere to merge crop intelligence with its existing precision agriculture equipment and technology.
The objective of this integration is to assist growers in making more informed decisions by linking crop-level data directly with field execution capabilities.
This action underscores John Deere's continued focus on embedding advanced artificial intelligence across its product offerings.
This strategic move signals a continued trend toward combining granular data with on-the-ground operational execution in agricultural technology.
From Robotics & Automation News, Viabot expands autonomous outdoor cleaning operations across eight US states.
This report details the expansion of the company's autonomous outdoor cleaning operations utilizing the Viabot One platform across eight US states.
The platform currently services twenty-five million square feet of commercial property, encompassing shopping centers and university campuses.
The robotic systems employ cameras, lidar, and GPS for autonomous navigation, debris collection, and property monitoring.
The system incorporates autonomous tool swapping and battery replacement capabilities, allowing for twelve to twenty-four hours of continuous operation.
Furthermore, the company recently secured twenty-four million dollars in Series A funding to facilitate further growth in its robotics-as-a-service business.
This development signals continued growth in the deployment of advanced robotics within commercial property management sectors.
From Humanoid.guide, "Samsung humanoid targets CES 2027 debut with 40 hand motors".
This report details Samsung's plan to debut its first humanoid robot at the Consumer Electronics Show in 2027, featuring forty hand motors designed for smartphone assembly tasks.
Development is being led by the Hand Lab, which has utilized a direct drive mechanism and joint technology adapted from Galaxy hinges for the robot's hands.
Two models, designated HR and HE, are in development, with the goal of integrating the humanoid into factory automation for production equipment management and assembly by the year 2030.
A substantial investment of nineteen trillion won is allocated for establishing a humanoid mass production system and necessary data infrastructure in Gumi.
This initiative signals a focused effort by Samsung to advance physical robotics within the industrial automation sector.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Flying race cars take to the skies as Airspeeder partners with Advanced Navigation".
This report details the launch of a racing series featuring electric flying cars and the collaboration with Advanced Navigation for flight control technology.

The initiative involves Airspeeder launching a racing series with electric flying cars capable of exceeding one hundred twenty kilometers per hour, controlled remotely through augmented reality interfaces.
Advanced Navigation has supplied the necessary precision positioning and flight control systems to facilitate this endeavor.

The inaugural race is scheduled for November two thousand twenty-six in Adelaide, Australia, involving five international pilots who will navigate virtual racetracks overlaid onto real-world environments in three dimensions.
This partnership functions as an experimental platform for advancing autonomous aviation technologies.
The development indicates a progression in remote control and autonomous flight systems for future aerial vehicle applications.
From turingpost.com, "AI 101 | Turing Post"

provides weekly explainer series on AI concepts for engineers focusing on underlying mechanisms rather than metaphors and explores topics including embodied AI for robot agents and the mechanics of LLM inference.

The series details the exploration of topics such as Looped Transformers test-time training and the architecture of AI agents, frequently addressing practical applications like skill engineering for agents and the infrastructure of Responsible AI.
The content tracks research in world models retrieval and AI infrastructure.
This ongoing analysis provides an engineering foundation for understanding the operational mechanisms within advanced artificial intelligence systems.
The developments in this area inform the practical deployment and infrastructure development of future AI technologies.

From turingpost.com, Twitter Library or Turing Post curates AI-related content focusing on model architectures, reinforcement learning approaches, JEPA, and agentic memory through infographics and guides.
The library provides precise analysis of research and systems shaping the field of machine learning and artificial intelligence.

The content frequently addresses methods to speed up vision-language agent actions, video generation techniques, and tools for computer-use AI agents, incorporating research on Looped Transformers, attention mechanisms, and AI guardrails for large language models.
Specific topics covered include embodied AI, robotics advancements, and the frameworks for building sophisticated AI agents.
This curated collection presents detailed analysis of the systems driving current machine learning and AI development.
Future developments in embodied systems and agentic frameworks will be reflected in this material.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Schindler escalators provide mountain access at 2,300 meters in China".
This report details how six Schindler escalators have provided access to the scenic peaks of Longtoushan, located over 2,300 meters above sea level, for a duration of seven years.

The outdoor escalator system, approximately 170 meters in length, was implemented to address accessibility difficulties in the harsh mountain environment characterized by heavy snowfall and low temperatures.
Schindler integrated specific anti-freezing and heating systems into the apparatus to maintain reliable operation in the extreme climate.
This project illustrates the application of vertical transportation technology in creating access to remote and challenging environments.
This development signals advancements in engineering solutions for extreme environment accessibility.
From Hackaday - Robots, "A Dozen Completely DIY Robot Actuators"
reports on the creation of a set of custom robot actuator motors.
The project demonstrates a methodology for significantly reducing the cost of robot components through modular design.
The development involved Koshiro Robot creating a dozen custom robot actuator motors, complete with their drivers and Field-Oriented Control firmware.
These actuators feature a 3D-printed gearbox and motor controller situated outside the stator to facilitate improved cooling and simplified wiring.
Power and signal distribution are managed via CAN-bus-plus-XT-60 daisy chaining.
This design strategy allows for cost multiplication by producing multiple identical units efficiently.
This work showcases an experimentalist-friendly approach to lowering the expense of robotic hardware.
The successful implementation suggests a pathway for democratizing access to cost-effective robotic components in future developments.
From Humanoids Daily, Figure and T-Mobile Bring F.03 Humanoids to the Las Vegas Grand Prix.
This report details the appearance of Figure and T-Mobile's F.03 humanoids at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, where the robots were featured on the circuit and in the pit lane.
The robots were observed walking the track and pit lane while wearing co-branded vests displaying the event and company logos.
This appearance represents a transition from previous demonstrations in industrial and residential environments.
Specific details concerning the robots' role for spectators and the commercial terms of the partnership were not disclosed.
This event signals an expansion of the presence of humanoid robotics into high-profile public and entertainment settings.
And that's all the circuits for today!
Hope your day is fully optimized.
Keep building those brilliant ideas, and we'll see you tomorrow for more robot revelations.
Bye for now!
